Collaborate with global network, security, cloud, and application teams to deliver end-to-end infrastructure solutions. Create and maintain global architecture documentation, operational standards, and runbooks. Participate in on-call and shift-based rotations as part of a 24 7 follow-the-sun operations model. Professional & Technical Skills: 3+ years of experience in enterprise or global data center operations. Strong expertise in VMware technologies including vSphere, vCenter, NSX, and Aria vRealize Operations. Hands-on experience with x86 server infrastructures from Dell, HPE, and Lenovo. In-depth knowledge of Brocade SAN fabrics, zoning, and enterprise-scale SAN design. Strong experience with NetApp storage solutions including NAS, MetroCluster, replication, and cloning. Experience with NetApp StorageGRID and object storage architectures. Hands-on experience with Pure Storage platforms including FlashArray and FlashBlade. Solid understanding of enterprise backup, recovery, and business continuity using Commvault Backup & Recovery. Scripting skills in Python and PowerShell for automation and operational tooling. Strong hands-on experience with Ansible for automated configuration management and deployment. Experience with GitLab CI/CD pipelines and infrastructure-as-code (IaC) methodologies. Strong knowledge of high availability, disaster recovery, and resilience design. Ability to work effectively in globally distributed teams with strong communication skills. Fluent English communication skills. Additional Information: The candidate should have minimum 3 years of experience in Storage Area Networks (SAN) Architecture and Design. review_candidates.title: Cybersecurity Specialist
review_candidates.description: Job Title: Cybersecurity Specialist Job Category: Information Technology Time Type: Full time Minimum Clearance Required to Start: Secret Employee Type: Regular Percentage of Travel Required: Up to 10% Type of Travel: Local * * * The Opportunity Join a team dedicated to protecting critical enterprise systems and supporting secure global operations through cybersecurity engineering, information assurance, and risk management. As a Cybersecurity Specialist, you will help safeguard mission-critical technology by implementing security controls, assessing cyber risk, supporting compliance efforts, and strengthening the security posture of enterprise infrastructure operating across worldwide environments. This requisition supports multiple experience levels—from professionals building foundational cybersecurity expertise to senior technical leaders responsible for designing secure architectures, managing cybersecurity programs, and leading enterprise risk management initiatives. Successful candidates will collaborate with engineering, operations, cloud, networking, and Government stakeholders to ensure systems remain secure, resilient, and compliant throughout their lifecycle. If you enjoy solving complex security challenges, protecting enterprise environments, and contributing to high-impact national security missions, this is an opportunity to make a meaningful difference while advancing your cybersecurity career. Opportunities available upon contract award Responsibilities Depending on experience and level, responsibilities may include: Implement, maintain, and assess cybersecurity controls across enterprise IT systems, cloud environments, applications, and network infrastructure. Support Risk Management Framework (RMF) activities throughout the system lifecycle, including authorization packages, security documentation, assessments, and continuous monitoring. Develop, review, and maintain System Security Plans (SSPs), Security Assessment Reports (SARs), Plans of Action and Milestones (POA&Ms), security policies, procedures, and supporting documentation. Conduct security assessments, vulnerability analysis, compliance reviews, and risk assessments to identify and mitigate cybersecurity threats. Coordinate vulnerability remediation efforts with engineering and operations teams while tracking corrective actions to completion. Monitor enterprise security posture using cybersecurity tools, vulnerability scanners, endpoint protection platforms, and security monitoring solutions. Support security accreditation activities, audits, inspections, and compliance reporting. Evaluate proposed system changes to determine security impacts and recommend appropriate safeguards. Participate in incident response activities, forensic support, root cause analysis, and lessons learned documentation. Collaborate with system administrators, network engineers, cloud engineers, software developers, and Government stakeholders to integrate cybersecurity throughout system design and operations. Support implementation of Zero Trust principles, cloud security best practices, identity and access management, encryption, and secure configuration standards. Develop security metrics, dashboards, and reports to communicate cybersecurity performance and risk. Senior-level professionals may lead cybersecurity engineering efforts, oversee RMF activities, serve as Information System Security Officers (ISSOs), mentor junior staff, and advise Government leadership on enterprise cybersecurity strategy and compliance. Required Qualifications Qualifications vary based on position level. High School diploma with relevant experience or bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Assurance, Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related technical discipline. Active Secret Clearance Experience supporting cybersecurity, information assurance, system security engineering, network security, or information systems security. Knowledge of cybersecurity principles, risk management, security controls, and secure system design. Familiarity with vulnerability management, security monitoring, and cybersecurity best practices. Experience developing technical documentation and communicating cybersecurity risks to technical and non-technical stakeholders. Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to obtain and maintain any required Government security clearance. Desired Qualifications Experience supporting Federal Government or Department of State cybersecurity programs. Experience serving as an Information System Security Officer (ISSO) or Information System Security Manager (ISSM). Experience implementing the NIST Risk Management Framework (RMF) and supporting Authority to Operate (ATO) processes. Familiarity with NIST SP 800-53, NIST SP 800-171, FISMA, FedRAMP, and other Federal cybersecurity standards. Experience with vulnerability management tools such as Tenable Nessus, Tenable Security Center, Qualys, or similar platforms. Experience using security information and event management (SIEM) tools such as Microsoft Sentinel, Splunk Enterprise Security, IBM QRadar, or Microsoft Defender XDR. Knowledge of cloud security technologies supporting Microsoft Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud Platform (GCP). Experience supporting endpoint security, identity and access management (IAM), multi-factor authentication (MFA), PKI, and privileged access management (PAM). This position is contingent on funding and may not be filled immediately. However, this position is representative of positions within CACI that are consistently available. Individuals who apply may also be considered for other positions at CACI. What You Can Expect A culture of integrity. At CACI, we place character and innovation at the center of everything we do. As a valued team member, you’ll be part of a high-performing group dedicated to our customer’s missions and driven by a higher purpose – to ensure the safety of our nation. An environment of trust. CACI values the unique contributions that every employee brings to our company and our customers - every day. You’ll have the autonomy to take the time you need through a unique flexible time off benefit and have access to robust learning resources to make your ambitions a reality. A focus on continuous growth. Together, we will advance our nation's most critical missions, build on our lengthy track record of business success, and find opportunities to break new ground — in your career and in our legacy. Pay Range There are a host of factors that can influence final salary including, but not limited to, geographic location, Federal Government contract labor categories and contract wage rates, relevant prior work experience, specific skills and competencies, education, and certifications. Our employees value the flexibility at CACI that allows them to balance quality work and their personal lives. We offer competitive compensation, benefits and learning and development opportunities. Our broad and competitive mix of benefits options is designed to support and protect employees and their families. At CACI, you will receive comprehensive benefits such as; healthcare, wellness, financial, retirement, family support, continuing education, and time off benefits. The Proposed Salary Range For This Position Is $103,800 - $218,100 CACI is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, status as a protected veteran, or any other protected characteristic.

We offer innovative, efficient and sustainable solutions for customers in industries where controlling indoor humidity, temperature and energy efficiency is mission critical. Climate control systems often account for a large percentage of energy consumption in many of our customers’ operations. With an optimal climate system, we can help them to more efficiently use energy or water resources and thereby reduce their climate and environmental impact. Sustainability is an important part of Munters’ business strategy and value creation. It supports troubleshooting, commissioning activities, warranty assessments, technical documentation and continuous improvement initiatives. Identify spare parts and spare part numbers including alternative parts where original parts are unavailable or obsolete. Organise and maintain technical libraries including but no limited to, technical manuals, technical bulletins and technical information received from third party vendors. review_candidates.title: Infrastructure & Operations Manager
review_candidates.description: If interested in this opportunity, please visit our website to read the full announcement. Applications closes on 09/10/2026. Hello, we’re Metro ! Metro is dedicated to shaping a better future for the greater Portland region. The work the people of Metro do every day benefits the lives of the people who live here, today, and tomorrow. The Information Technology department is looking for an Infrastructure & Operations Manager to lead the teams that run the technology foundation the rest of the organization relies on. Metro is responsible for regional planning, garbage and recycling, conserving natural areas, providing parks, and operating the Portland Expo Center, the Oregon Convention Center, and the Oregon Zoo. The infrastructure behind it works across the offices, venues, transfer stations, and parks. Providing Metro's variety of services with resilient and reliable technology is a point of pride for our team. Today Metro runs a hybrid environment: on-premises infrastructure alongside cloud services, hybrid identity, a Microsoft enterprise stack, and endpoints spanning all our locations. The environment is stable and well cared for, built and run by a team with deep knowledge of Metro's systems.  The future of infrastructure and operations is being reshaped by automation and AI, and Metro is investing in that future: in stronger service management, in automation that takes on routine work so people can focus their expertise where it matters most, and in AI-assisted ways of working. Every choice along the way gets weighed by whether it makes the work more reliable and the team more capable.  We're looking for a leader who can take us there. Someone who has strengthened an infrastructure team's practices and readiness for what's next, and who leads as a team player. Someone who takes Metro's goals as their own, partnering with the departments and venues we serve so their needs drive the work, all while keeping our essential technology services on and available. If that sounds like you, we would like to hear from you. As the Infrastructure & Operations Manager you will Lead Metro's Systems and Support teams, 14 staff across systems administration and help desk, through two direct-report supervisors.  Keep Metro's systems dependable and secure, so the people of Metro can rely on technology to do their work. Your teams run on-call, and major incident escalation ends with you.  Strengthen the resilience and availability of Metro's systems, including backup and disaster recovery, so critical services hold up through disruption.  Mature Metro's IT service management, building the change, incident, and problem practices that make service measurable, responsive, and steadily improving.  Bring modern practices into everyday operations: infrastructure and configuration as code, observability that catches issues before users report them, and shared documentation that makes systems easier for the whole team to support.  Own the life cycle and architecture of Metro's systems: deciding whether to modernize, consolidate, migrate, or retire, and where each workload should run.  Lead the practical, responsible adoption of AI and other innovations in operations, and help your teams build the skills to harness this tool.  Partner with Metro's cybersecurity leadership to run infrastructure that meets Metro's information security needs.  Work across Metro's departments and venues, translating technology decisions into terms the people who rely on them can understand and trust.  Develop and manage the infrastructure and operations budget, set vendor and contracting strategy, and get strong value from Metro's technology investments.  Keep capacity ahead of demand: knowing what the team should own, what's better handled by vendors and partners, and how the mix should shift as needs change.  Own Metro's major infrastructure initiatives and capital investments: making the case for them, delivering what was promised, and being accountable for the value they return. Attributes for success You've led an infrastructure team through modernization, consolidations, or migrations, while the systems stayed up and the work of the organization carried on.  You have a strong foundation in enterprise systems, networking, storage, and identity, and you're credible with the system administrators who run them.  You know the Microsoft ecosystem deeply, on-premises and cloud, including licensing and endpoints, and you keep it evolving as the organization's needs change.  You've made a service operation measurably better, implementing service management practices that made a difference, and it stayed better after you moved on to the next thing.  You've led through real incidents: keeping your head while systems are down, running a blameless review after, and making fixes that mean the same failure doesn't repeat.  You find places to automate repetitive work in your team through scripts, pipelines, or configuration, and you can say what you automated first and why, because you'd rather find a better way than to keep doing it manually.  You scale process to risk: changes with real blast radius get real controls, and routine work doesn't get buried under them.  You give people ownership, clear what's in their way, and grow their skills, and it shows in your team: people who work well together and like the work.  You're a strong collaborator, with the teams you work beside and the people who depend on your services, and they bring you into problems early.  Your organizational skills let you keep daily operations, projects, budget, and vendors all moving, and your team still gets to the quiet yet crucial work like patching, backup testing, and lifecycle replacement.  You have demonstrated experience with IT vendor, service, and contract management to get the most value for IT services. TO QUALIFY We will consider any combination of relevant work experience, volunteering, education, and transferable skills as qualifying unless an item or section is labeled required. Please be clear and specific in your application materials on how your background is relevant.  Minimum qualifications Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, and Five (5) years of experience leading or supervising technical staff or teams in IT infrastructure or IT operations, and Two (2) years of experience managing IT infrastructure projects or initiatives, such as migrations, consolidations, upgrades, or system implementations, or Any combination of education, professional, volunteer and lived experience that provides the necessary knowledge, skills, and abilities to perform the classification duties and responsibilities. Hybrid Telework  This position is designated as “hybrid telework.” You will be required to work onsite and at times have the option to work away from your assigned work location. The specific schedule and balance of onsite and telework will be discussed with the hiring manager at the time of offer. Employees must reside in Oregon or Washington to work at Metro. Please note, the designation of hybrid telework may be subject to change at a future time. This position supports systems that operate outside business hours, including at Metro's venues. Travel between Metro locations, evening and weekend work, and extended hours may be required.  The teams this position leads provide on-call coverage. During major incidents and emergencies, this position may be required to report onsite on short notice. Like to have qualifications You do not need to have the following preferred qualifications/transferable skills to qualify. However, keep in mind we may consider them when identifying the most qualified candidates. Your transferable skills are any skills you have gained through education, work experience, including the military, or life experience that are relevant for this position. Training or certification in an IT service management framework or methodology, such as ITIL, COBIT, or an equivalent. Experience in government or another highly regulated industry, such as healthcare, utilities, or financial services. Experience leading or working within a union-represented workforce. Demonstrated use of AI tools in your own work, and experience bringing a team along in adopting them. COMPENSATION, BENEFITS AND REPRESENTATON The full-salary range for this position is step 1: $134,836.98 to step 6: $172,089.69. However, unless a candidate’s qualifications justify, based on the Oregon Pay Equity Act requirements and Metro’s internal equity review process, the appointment will likely be made between step 1: $134,836.98 to the equity range step 4: $156,091.17.  This position is not eligible for overtime and is non-represented. It is classified as a Manager II position. Classification descriptions are typically written broadly and do not include the specific duties and responsibilities of the positions. View the classification description. Questions? Ability to establish/maintain good working relationships and be able to work cooperatively/productively with engineers, vendors, and customers is required. Strong ability to troubleshoot software problems - identify and solve problems creatively and effectively. Ability to learn and understand new processes, as well as recommend ways to continuously improve. Experience working in a broader enterprise/cross-division business unit model preferred Ability to work in a highly matrixed and geographically diverse business environment. Ability to work within a team and as an individual contributor in a fast paced, changing environment. Ability to leverage and/or engage others to accomplish projects. Strong verbal and written communications with ability to effectively communicate at multiple levels in the organization. Multitasks, prioritizes, and meets deadlines in a timely manner. Strong organizational and follow-up skills, as well as attention to detail. Experience as a Programmer with SQL language as well as an object-oriented language (C# or equivalent). Experience with RDMS such as Oracle, SQL Server, MS-SQL, etc. Experience with reporting tools (Crystal Reports, Tableau) and with web technologies such as Web Services, API, HTML, CSS and JavaScript is desired. Based in Singapore, with a valid driving licence or ability to travel independently; willing and able to attend customer sites within Singapore and be onsite within the contractual SLA during business hours. Fluency in oral and written English. Ability to speak a local language in addition to English is a strong plus. Nice to have: Prior LIMS, ELN, SDMS or LES experience Candidates must currently hold valid Singapore work authorization (e.g., Singapore Citizen, Permanent Resident, or an eligible working pass) STARLIMS is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history. At the heart of Defining Possible is our commitment to missions. In rapidly changing global security environments, Northrop Grumman brings informed insights and software-secure technology to enable strategic planning. We’re looking for innovators who can help us keep building on our wide portfolio of secure, affordable, integrated, and multi-domain systems and technologies that fuel those missions. By joining in our shared mission, we’ll support yours of expanding your personal network and developing skills, whether you are new to the field, or an industry thought leader. At Northrop Grumman, you’ll have the resources, support, and team to do some of the best work of your career. Qualified candidates will apply strong systems engineering knowledge and understanding in the areas of target tracking, state estimation, and sensor fusion, working with various systems, hardware, and software teams. We encourage our engineers to be innovative with solving problems and identifying improvements. This position requires up to 100% on-site What You’ll Get To Do This position is primarily engaged in the development and fielding of target tracking and sensor fusion systems for advanced multi-function RF subsystems. Key features of operation include analyzing, shaping, and relating data from a wide variety of modes, such as: long-range search and track Radar waveforms and electronic surveillance measure returns. Early in the system lifecycle, Principal systems engineers develop parametric representations, visualizations and data driven analysis to support sensor requirements definition and use case validation. Progressing past analysis and design, Northrop Grumman Systems Engineers also support the integration of sensor modes and trackers from digital simulation environments to sensor labs to our on-site fleet of specially modified test aircraft. Throughout this process, our AMS Systems Engineers engage with our customers to balance their functional and performance requirements with other sensor functionality to enable true multi-function operation. Operates as a core individual contributor responsible for the sustained performance and minor adaptation of established algorithms and systems. Execute technical tasks under general supervision, focusing on maintaining existing functionalities and making incremental improvements within clearly defined boundaries. Ensures current systems meet performance objectives by leveraging existing documentation, such as defined Interface Control Documents (ICDs). Utilize foundational skills in MATLAB and C++ for basic analysis and code modifications. U.S Citizenship is required. A current/active U.S. Government Secret Clearance Ability to obtain Special Program Access (SAP) prior to start Experience with multi-target tracking, adaptive processing, or sensor fusion algorithms Experience with MATLAB or equivalent programming/analysis languages Experience with RF signals processing or RF applications Experience with working knowledge of systems engineering principles and processes and effective communication skills. Has been previously approved for special access programs.
